title: Audit exporter: Splunk HEC destination adapter (auth, batching, 429 handling, index/source/sourcetype)
creator: Rafael Mendes
description: Implement Splunk HEC destination adapter for SIEM-ready audit export beta. Requirements: secure token-based auth, configurable index/source/sourcetype, event batching to control throughput/cost, and robust handling of Splunk-side throttling (429) with backoff + circuit breaking. Must preserve at-least-once semantics (ADR) and provide actionable metrics/logs for SRE/support.
acceptance_criteria:
- Exporter can deliver audit events to Splunk HEC /services/collector/event with valid token and endpoint.
- Destination config supports customer-configurable index/source/sourcetype (optional; defaults applied safely).
- Adapter batches events (size/time based) and supports gzip compression.
- 429/503/timeout handling: exponential backoff with jitter, honors Retry-After when present, and does not hot-loop.
- Per-destination circuit breaker prevents flooding Splunk and protects exporter resources.
- Adapter produces metrics for request success/failures, 429 count, retries, dropped-to-DLQ count, and batch sizes.
- Unit tests cover payload formatting, batching boundaries, Retry-After behavior, and error classification.
- Integration test harness validates delivery against Splunk sandbox/stub.
- No token/PII leakage in logs; secrets sourced via secret reference (not plaintext).
implementation_notes:
Protocol / endpoint:
- Use Splunk HEC JSON event endpoint: POST https://<hec_host>:8088/services/collector/event
- Header: Authorization: Splunk <token>
- Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
- Optional: Content-Encoding: gzip (enabled by default for batches > ~4KB)

Event format:
- Use HEC "event" field to embed Redwood audit event object (schema v2) as JSON.
- Set HEC top-level fields when configured: "index", "source", "sourcetype".
- Time mapping: set top-level "time" (epoch seconds with millis precision when available) derived from audit_event.occurred_at; keep original timestamps inside event payload as well.
- Host mapping: use exporter runtime host id / region tag (do not set to customer hostnames).

Batching:
- Batch flush conditions: max_events (default 250), max_bytes (default 512KB pre-compression), max_delay (default 1s).
- HEC supports multiple JSON objects separated by newline in a single request; adapter emits NDJSON where each line is a complete HEC event envelope.
- Preserve ordering per destination where possible, but do not block other tenants/destinations.

Retries / throttling / circuit breaker:
- Classify retryable: network errors, 408/429/500/502/503/504.
- Honor Retry-After header (seconds) on 429 when present; otherwise exponential backoff with full jitter.
- Implement per-destination circuit breaker keyed by destination_id (and implicitly token): open after N consecutive throttles/errors; half-open after cool-down; close on success.
- Ensure at-least-once semantics: if request fails after max attempts, batch goes to DLQ with checkpoint not advanced.

Config surface:
- Destination settings: hec_url (base), hec_token_secret_ref, index (optional), source (optional), sourcetype (optional), tls_verify (default true).
- Validate hec_url scheme https only (http rejected), and reject URLs with paths other than /services/collector or /services/collector/event (normalize /event).
- Ensure index/source/sourcetype length constraints and character sanity (Splunk-side validation is inconsistent; we fail fast on obvious invalid values).

Observability:
- Metrics (prom): audit_exporter_adapter_requests_total{adapter="splunk",status="success|error",code="...",destination_id="..."}; audit_exporter_adapter_retries_total; audit_exporter_adapter_throttled_total; audit_exporter_batch_events; audit_exporter_batch_bytes.
- Structured logs include destination_id, tenant_id, batch_id, attempt, http_status, splunk_ack (if present); never include token or full event payload.

Security / privacy:
- Token is treated as secret; only secret ref stored in control plane config.
- Explicit redaction: prevent logging Authorization header; sanitize any response bodies.
- Confirm payload adheres to audit event PII policy (schema v2 + redaction rules). Adapter should not add new user PII fields beyond what schema already permits.

Customer expectations (beta):
- Delivery is at-least-once; customer must deduplicate using event_id (and/or event_id + occurred_at) on Splunk side.
- During prolonged Splunk throttling/outage, exporter will accumulate lag and may auto-pause per backpressure controls; recovery will replay (possible duplicates).
rollout_plan:
Feature-flag gated (tenant allowlist).
1) Enable for internal dogfood tenant with Splunk sandbox.
2) Enable for 1 beta customer (Acme Banking) with close monitoring of throttling/lag.
3) Gradually enable remaining beta cohort after SRE sign-off on alert noise and circuit breaker behavior.
Rollback: disable destination in control plane (pause exports) and/or flip kill switch flag for tenant; batches remain in queue/DLQ for replay after fix.
testing_plan:
Unit tests:
- Builds HEC envelope correctly with/without index/source/sourcetype
- NDJSON batching formatting and max_bytes boundary
- Retry-After parsing and backoff floor/ceiling
- Error classification for retryable vs permanent

Integration tests:
- Run against Splunk sandbox (docker) from exporter harness; validate events arrive and are searchable by sourcetype/index.
- Inject 429 responses; verify backoff + no hot-loop; verify circuit breaker opens.
- Verify auth failures (401/403) surface as permanent errors and do not retry indefinitely.

Load-ish validation:
- Replay synthetic audit events at target beta rate; confirm exporter CPU/memory stable and Splunk HEC does not get hammered on throttling.
comments: 2025-02-06 (Rafael Mendes): Splunk is the gating integration for Acme Banking. Please prioritize 429 handling; they rate limit aggressively and we need to avoid a thundering herd + noisy paging.

2025-02-10 (Diego Santos): Plan: implement adapter as separate package under destinations/ with shared retry/backoff util. Will use NDJSON batching for HEC. Need decision on defaults for index/source/sourcetype; proposing: leave unset unless customer config provides (Splunk default index applies).

2025-02-11 (Marcus Lin): Security note: do not log response bodies verbatim; Splunk error bodies sometimes echo submitted event fragments. Please scrub. Token must be secret ref only; no plaintext in config snapshots.
2025-02-14 (Sean Gallagher): Add metric specifically for throttles (429) and a panel showing throttle rate vs lag; this is likely the top failure mode in beta.

2025-02-18 (Diego Santos): Implemented Retry-After support + full jitter backoff. Added per-destination circuit breaker (opens on consecutive 429/5xx). Working through exact open/half-open thresholds with SRE.

2025-02-24 (Colin O'Donnell): Customer request: ability to set sourcetype to something stable for dashboards, e.g., redwood:audit. Also prefer setting source to "redwood". Please confirm adapter supports all three fields.
2025-03-04 (Diego Santos): PR up with adapter + config validation + metrics. Integration test harness wired to Splunk docker. Awaiting Security review on logging redaction and secret plumbing.
2025-03-07 (Kevin Osei): Confirmed: payload must include event_id and occurred_at; customer will dedup on event_id. Please ensure we never mutate event_id when re-serializing.

2025-03-12 (Diego Santos): Merged. Follow-up needed to tune default batch sizes for Splunk HEC (some customers cap request size lower). Tracking tuning in SRE experiment doc + will open separate ticket if needed.
outcome: Adapter implemented and merged with batching, configurable index/source/sourcetype, Retry-After aware backoff, and per-destination circuit breaker. Metrics added for throttles/retries to support beta operations.
